session.title: 1.0.38: refresh on exit resumes the window's own Codex conversation (SW208)
session.purpose: Carry out SW208: a Codex window queued for refresh on exit came back on Codex's conversation picker; the user wants it back on the conversation it was showing, never another window's (several windows often share one folder, so --last is wrong). Resume that window's own conversation, release 1.0.38, install it on the workstation and verify live.
outcomes: Item 1: while a refresh on exit is queued, Switchy reads the threads loaded on the window's own app-server (thread/loaded/list + thread/read) and writes the one conversation with a message to <window>.thread beside the session file, leaving out the empty thread a window starts with, the ephemeral title thread and subagent threads (parentThreadId set). It re-reads every 2 s and on thread/started or thread/status/changed. The PowerShell wrapper and the WSL function read that id after the client exits and run 'codex resume <id>' with the window's launch options; with none or several conversations, or an id that is not UUID-shaped, the picker opens. Probed first: a window's server keeps every conversation it opened loaded after the client exits, and broadcasts thread/started to every connection.

Item 2: two new tests in proxy::codex_engine (choosing the window's conversation among launch, title and subagent threads, none, two, a non-id; the name file against a fake window server: named while queued, removed on cancel, removed when the window closes). cargo test --lib proxy::codex_engine: 12 passed.

Item 3: v1.0.38 released on registered2nd/switchy (Latest) with the exe and msi, digests matching installers/, target public 492b772d. The Apple Silicon DMG was skipped at the user's direction because a GitHub Actions incident (opened 08:49 local) left build-macos.yml run 39281410009 and the push's Tests run 39281394998 queued with no runner; the release notes and README point Mac users to the 1.0.37 DMG (the change only touches the Windows and WSL codex shells). Cancelling run 39281410009 was refused as 'completed' while GitHub still listed it queued. Installed on the workstation by the one-command reinstall at 08:54:33 local, port 15721 up in 1 s. Not updated: the laptop and another user's Mac (1.0.36), another user's PC (1.0.36 installed, not running).

Item 4: verified live in Windows and WSL with two windows in one scratch folder each. Windows: A (ECHO, 01a154df-7604-70d3-b6ef-90bceb29d94f) queued over /switchy/invoke, logged 'refresh on exit resumes conversation 01a154df-7604...', came back with 'codex --remote ws://127.0.0.1:53313 ... resume 01a154df-7604...', its message in history, no picker; B (FOXTROT) unchanged. WSL: A (GOLF, 01a154e3-908d-72f1-a4f1-5ebe39f9cf85) came back with 'codex --remote unix://.../620622-6334.sock resume 01a154e3-908d...'; B (HOTEL) unchanged. Test windows exited, their files gone, scratch folders removed by literal path; 0 'actively refused' lines and 0 codex_engine warnings since the install.

Side effect, reported: the first WSL test window showed Codex's update prompt and the Enter meant for the test message chose 'Update now', which ran 'npm install -g @openai/codex' in WSL: the WSL Codex CLI went from 0.162.1 to 0.163.0 (same as Windows) at 08:56 local. The WSL window open since 04:46 (91020-17871.sock) still runs its 0.162.1 server, so Pool settings will show it as out of date.

Found and reported to the hub, not fixed: on Windows, closing an exploration terminal without Codex exiting left its hidden app-server running (port 55741) for 10 minutes, so its files stayed; it was stopped by hand and Switchy then forgot it. Whether Orca's tab close takes the server with it was not checked. Stale WSL socket links (5) and the three unused-import warnings remain as in 1.0.37.
session.latest_summary: 1.0.38 brings a Codex window queued for refresh on exit back on its own conversation, in Windows and WSL, falling back to the picker when the window has no single conversation. Released with Windows installers only (the DMG was skipped during a GitHub Actions incident); installed and verified live on the workstation only.

next_actions.summary: Confirm account-proxy coverage on the next natural Claude sign-in or renewal while Owen is selected, without forcing a new login. Claude Code's own exchange should log '[connect_tunnel] platform.claude.com:443 via socks5://82.26.163.142:45001'. For Switchy's renewal, observe '[claude_pool] refreshing login for provider=98e00f12...' and the successful refreshed-login message; the enforced per-account client route is owned by proxy/http_client.rs. Windows/WSL HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY, UK exit probes and telemetry tunnels were verified; a live sign-in/renewal using this route remains unobserved. Connection failures must stop rather than fall back to direct; country observations only warn.

CONFIRM THE RESTART PATH ON STEPHEN'S NEXT WINDOWS RESTART (1.0.29). In C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.prev.log after 'Session ending; handing the live configs back': '[session-end] claude/codex/gemini handed back', '[session-end] ... in WSL handed back', then 'Live configs handed back for the session end'. 'did not finish in 4 seconds' with the last [session-end] line shows which step stalls (Windows step = database lock, WSL step = WSL I/O); fix that step. In switchy.log: Switchy started within seconds of login (window hidden, launched with --autostart from HKCU Run), '[auto_launch] start at login on', proxy on 15721, and Claude Code / Codex answer without ECONNREFUSED.

CONFIRM CLAUDE LOGINS STAY IN STEP WITH WSL (1.0.27). In switchy.log, when an account WSL is signed in to renews: '[claude_pool] provider=... took the newer login from WSL' or 'wrote the refreshed login through to WSL', and no new 'invalid_grant' 'Refresh token not found or invalid' in account_switches/provider_health. WSL's ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.switchy/accounts/<id>/credentials.json for that account should carry the same refreshToken after each renewal.

CONFIRM ROTATION AND CODEX FAILOVER ON LIVE TRAFFIC (1.0.25/1.0.26). In C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.log and the switchy.db account_switches table: (a) when an account's five-hour window resets while another serves, a switch back to it with reason 'recovered' and detail "Another account's weekly limit resets sooner"; (b) a Codex turn refused for usage that continues an earlier one logs '[CodexWS] provider=... websocket closed (turn refused for usage; Codex resends it in full)' and the turn then completes on the next account with no error in Codex. GET http://127.0.0.1:15721/switchy/accounts shows current account, pool order, quota and atLimit per account.

VERIFY LOCAL PROXY OFF WITH AN OPEN CODEX WINDOW. the user was asked to turn Local proxy off in Settings > Pool, then use a Codex window opened while the proxy was on. Confirm in C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.log that "Proxy turned off; its listener stays up..." was logged, that the Codex window's later [Codex] requests still reached the proxy and answered, that netstat shows 127.0.0.1:15721 still LISTENING, and that Settings shows the proxy as off. Turning it back on must reuse the listener.

QUIT CASE WAITS ON STEPHEN. Quitting Switchy still breaks Codex windows opened under the proxy. He was offered a warning on quit naming the open Codex windows (small) or running the proxy as a process that outlives Switchy's window (large); he has not chosen. Build nothing until he does.
If the user directs request logging to be enabled, first make the Usage page's Turn on button apply to the running proxy, then enable it for Claude, Codex, and Gemini.
